newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rates ease on election calm.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rates ease on election calm.

text.p: The surprising calm before the key July 6 elections in Mexico led to a surprisingly large decline in Cetes rates at the primary auction on Tuesday, analysts said.
The bellwether one-month rate, on Monday seen rising sharply, then seen rising only slightly before the auction, instead fell sharply, falling 95 basis points to 19.95 percent.
"People were most likely to jump into the short-end of the curve as the election risks were somewhat overblown," said IDEA economist Gene Frieda.
"It was either going to happen before or after the election and it appears they decided to be in before," he said.

Earlier concerns of a hike in U.S. interest at the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee meeting scheduled for this week have also evaporated, easing concerns of interest rate reverberations in Mexico.
A survey of nine money market dealers by Reuters earlier in the day found expectations of a rise of 18 basis points in the one-month paper but declines in longer-terms at the Banco de Mexico auction.
Many analysts had forecast market turmoil in the runup to the July 6 elections which will see a vote for Congress, for six state governors, part of the Senate and for a mayor in Mexico City.
But initial concerns that violence, particularly from guerrilla groups, could interrupt the election compaigns have proved largely groundless.
Moreover, the peso has remained relatively stable and the stock market has continued to post new highs, setting another record high on Tuesday.

"Each time around the election nervousness has waned until now they have more or less discounted the election results and are looking for a quiet outcome," said Santander Investment economist Enrique Ramirez.
He said that the possibility of an opposition victory in Mexico City had been discounted by markets as had fears of changes in economic policies.
"The market has already begun to read the elections as a non-problem, something that is not going to increase tensions," Ramirez said.
Demand rose sharply at the auction on Tuesday, increasing to 16.58 billion pesos from 14.35 billion pesos the week before.
